result.stdout:
Codebase intelligence for C#.

With no command, roe runs dead-code, dupes, and health together — the same thing as `roe check`.

Usage: roe [OPTIONS] [PATH]
       roe <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check      Run dead-code, dupes, and health together (the default when no command is given)
  dead-code  Find unused types, members, and files
  dupes      Find duplicated code blocks
  health     Flag complexity, size, and coupling issues
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Path to the codebase root (defaults to the current directory)

Options:
  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format
          
          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

      --config <PATH>
          Path to an explicit roe.json/roe.yaml/roe.yml config (skips auto-discovery)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

result.stdout:
Find duplicated code blocks

Usage: roe dupes [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Path to the codebase root (defaults to the current directory)

Options:
  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format
          
          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

      --mode <MODE>
          Matching mode

          Possible values:
          - exact:    Exact token match — only verbatim copy-pasted blocks match
          - semantic: Identifiers and numeric literals are normalized to a shared placeholder, so renamed-but-structurally-identical blocks match too
          
          [default: exact]

      --no-code
          Hide the duplicated source code printed under each group (human format only)

      --min-tokens <MIN_TOKENS>
          Minimum token-run length for a match to be reported
          
          [default: 50]

      --min-lines <MIN_LINES>
          Minimum line span (of the shortest occurrence) for a match to be reported
          
          [default: 5]

      --min-occurrences <MIN_OCCURRENCES>
          Minimum number of occurrences for a match to be reported
          
          [default: 2]

      --config <PATH>
          Path to an explicit roe.json/roe.yaml/roe.yml config (skips auto-discovery)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

result.stdout:
Flag complexity, size, and coupling issues

Usage: roe health [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Path to the codebase root (defaults to the current directory)

Options:
  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format
          
          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

      --max-complexity <MAX_COMPLEXITY>
          Flag methods/properties above this cyclomatic complexity [default: 10]

      --max-cognitive <MAX_COGNITIVE>
          Flag methods/properties above this cognitive complexity — like cyclomatic, but weighted by how deeply nested the code is [default: 15]

      --max-method-lines <MAX_METHOD_LINES>
          Flag methods/properties whose body spans more than this many lines [default: 40]

      --max-parameters <MAX_PARAMETERS>
          Flag methods/operators/indexers declared with more than this many parameters [default: 5]

      --max-file-lines <MAX_FILE_LINES>
          Flag files longer than this many lines [default: 750]

      --max-type-members <MAX_TYPE_MEMBERS>
          Flag types with more than this many members [default: 20]

      --exclude-tests
          Skip declarations in test projects — long arrange/act/assert methods and multi-case fixtures are normal there

      --sort <SORT>
          Order findings by how far past their threshold they sit, or by file path

          Possible values:
          - severity: Worst first, by how many times over its threshold each finding sits
          - path:     Grouped by file path, ascending — stable regardless of the metrics
          
          [default: severity]

      --limit <N>
          Print at most this many findings; 0 prints all of them
          
          [default: 0]

      --hotspots
          Also rank the files that are both complex and frequently changed, read from git history. Informational — never affects the exit code

      --top <TOP>
          How many hotspots to list
          
          [default: 10]

      --baseline <PATH>
          Report only findings that this baseline
[truncated]
